The golden tabby tiger, also known as the golden tiger, is an exceptionally rare color variation of the Bengal tiger. Its stunning coat is pale gold with faint orange stripes, caused by a recessive genetic mutation called chinchilla albinistic. These tigers are incredibly rare, with only about 30 known to exist, and they are found exclusively in captivity. Breeding programs in zoos and wildlife parks occasionally produce golden tabby tigers, but they are not seen in the wild due to their unique coloration, which reduces their camouflage and makes survival difficult.
